topic.title: Spirograph
topic.description: Creates a colorful spirograph pattern by drawing circles with a small heading change each iteration. Combines loops, geometry, and random color generation.

learningNotes.whatILearned: The spirograph: a turtle draws circles, turning a little further round each time, and the circles together make a rosette.
learningNotes.challenges: It needs tkinter, so it cannot run here — and there is no tkinter on Termux either.
learningNotes.nextSteps: Run it once on a machine with a screen and change the two numbers — 37 and 10 — until you can see why they produce the shape.

files.description: Colorful spirograph pattern with random RGB colors.

misconceptions: A spirograph is not one curve with a strange formula - it is many identical circles drawn with a turning offset
`setheading` sets an absolute angle; `right` adds to the current one - the shape depends on which one you use
engine.review:
**The rubric I used**

There is no task sheet for this one — it was written before the engine
existed, so there was nothing to grade it against. I graded the file on the
three things that have always mattered here:

- **40 — it runs.** It compiles or interprets without an error.
- **30 — it is right.** The output is what it claims to produce.
- **30 — it explains itself.** Comments say *why*, not *what*.

**0 + 30 + 5 = 35%**

**This file cannot be run here.** It needs `tkinter`, and this
machine has no display and no `tkinter`. The 40 points for *it runs* are
therefore not points I can give, and I do not give them.

The larger point: **`tkinter` does not exist on Termux either.** These
files cannot be run on the phone this whole system is built around. They
are not broken — they are stranded.

**What is right, by reading**

The maths is right, and it is a lovely piece of maths. The turtle draws a circle of radius 100, then turns 10 degrees further than last time and draws another; thirty-seven circles later, every one of them overlapping the others at a slightly different angle, and the whole thing comes out as a rosette. The heading is read *before* each circle (`current_heading = tim.heading()`) and then set to `current_heading + 10`, so the offset accumulates exactly as it should.

The two speeds are also right: `speed('fastest')` and a pen of width 5, because thirty-seven overlapping circles would take forever at normal speed.

**What is not**

**There are no comments**, and the two numbers that make the shape — 37 and 10 — are magic. A reader who changes one of them cannot predict what happens, and the number 10 is the actual subject of the file: a circle every 10 degrees, thirty-seven times.

The colour function has the same flaw as the one in `Random_color.py` — a local variable named the same as the function that returns it — and it is the same idea repeated, which is worth noticing: you wrote that shape twice.

There is also no explanation of why the turtle draws a *circle* instead of a polygon: `tim.circle(100)` draws an arc of that radius, and 360 degrees of it is a circle.

**The one thing to fix first**

Two comments on the two magic numbers:

```python
i = 0
while i < 37:            # How many circles to draw.
    tim.setheading(current_heading + 10)  # Each circle is drawn 10 degrees further round.
```

That pair of comments turns the file from a recipe into an explanation.
